A ratio's MAGNITUDE must account for the price discontinuity it is offered to explain. A split record whose ratio is too small to explain an observed move does not explain it -- MPP's 1-for-40 silenced a detector while the price moved 1,564x, which is the reason that test exists.

transformation_rule: Vendor snapshot date, falling back to the DATE THE TRANSFORM RAN when the source value is NULL.
business_rule:
THE FALLBACK DESTROYS THE DISTINCTION IT EXISTS TO RECORD. A row whose vendor snapshot date is unknown is written with today's date, so an undated figure becomes indistinguishable from one EODHD stamped this morning -- and the column consumers would use to judge currency is the one that cannot be trusted to show staleness.
A failed-to-obtain rendered as a confident value. NULL would have been the honest outcome; the column is already nullable.
Note also that `or` substitutes on any falsy value, not only None. For a date type NULL is the only falsy case, so the behaviour is correct today and would stop being correct if the column's type changed.
